column1: # conduck-connect WebDAV listing fixture corpus.
# corpus-version: 1
# Columns, TAB-separated: case, requested-url, wanted-entry,
# expected-verdict, parity. The body is <case>.xml in this directory,
# byte-exact and without a trailing newline. See README.md.
# The ordinary listing: the collection's own row plus one direct child.
child-direct
# A relative href resolves against the collection WITH its trailing slash,
# which is what makes it a child rather than a sibling.
child-relative
# A fully absolute href on the requested origin is the same child.
child-absolute-url
# A byte size changes no verdict. The app keeps it for the download chip; the
# mirror does not read it, and neither side's answer moves.
child-with-size
# Local names are matched with any prefix or none: a prefix is a serialization
# choice, and refusing one would refuse real servers.
namespace-unprefixed
# A path-stripping reverse proxy (Caddy handle_path, nginx proxy_pass with a
# trailing slash) hands the WebDAV server a shortened path, so the hrefs come
# back without the /box mount point. The match is anchored at the END of the
# requested path, so this reads; demanding the full prefix would refuse every
# row of a listing the app reads perfectly.
proxy-stripped-prefix
# A nested folder is dropped as undeliverable without touching the file beside
# it.
collection-beside-file
# One 404 propstat beside a 200 one still leaves a resource the server found:
# properties are read out of the successful propstat.
mixed-propstat
# Exactly listingMaxEntries responses is accepted — the bound is inclusive.
entries-at-cap
# Nesting exactly maxElementDepth deep is accepted.
depth-at-limit
# Exactly listingMaxBytes is accepted — the bound is inclusive.
bytes-at-limit
# A readable folder that simply does not hold the wanted name. ABSENT, never
# REFUSED: the two are different repairs on the operator's side.
absent-other-name
# A collection whose only row is itself.
empty-collection
# The wanted name is a folder. A nested folder is not a deliverable.
collection-child
# RFC 4918 lets a 207 carry rows about resources the server does NOT have.
# Emitting one as an entry would offer a file that is not there.
notfound-propstat
# The same rule at the response level rather than the propstat level.
notfound-response-status
# A response that states nothing about the resource is not evidence that the
# resource is there.
response-without-propstat
# A tail match is not a free-for-all: an EMPTY parent matches only an empty
# requested path, so a server answering about its own root cannot satisfy
# every listing.
proxy-served-root
# The parent must be a TAIL of the requested path, never a subsequence of it:
# a same-named folder under a different mount is refused.
proxy-wrong-mount
# A row about the parent directory is not describing the folder asked about.
parent-href
# Exactly one component past the folder, so a grandchild refuses the whole
# body rather than being dropped — a server must not hand over a curated
# subset of a listing the client believes is complete.
grandchild
# An href on another host is not describing the configured file server,
# whatever it claims about the path.
foreign-origin
# The path is split into components BEFORE each is decoded, so an escape that
# decodes to a separator or a dot segment cannot smuggle a second component
# past the direct-child test.
percent-encoded-dot-segment
# A response below anything but multistatus REFUSES the body. RFC 4918 puts it
# exactly one level down, so a deeper one is a row nobody understood, and
# dropping it would report a file that exists as an empty folder.
nested-response
# Exactly one href per response. None means the row names nothing.
response-without-href
# Two hrefs mean the row names two things, and nobody here decides which.
two-hrefs
# A control-UI HTML page answering a PROPFIND is not a listing.
not-multistatus-root
# A document that does not parse to completion is refused: a truncated listing
# is indistinguishable from a real short one.
truncated
# Malformed XML, refused rather than salvaged.
mismatched-tag
# An empty 207 body states nothing.
empty-body
# One level past maxElementDepth. A body nested deeper than a flat collection
# needs is doing something other than listing a directory.
depth-over-limit
# The two spellings of café — NFC U+00E9, and NFD e + U+0301 — are ONE name
# under Unicode canonical equivalence, which is what Swift string equality is.
# One real collection cannot hold two entries under one name, so the folder
# refuses. A code-point comparison would grade it an ordinary two-entry
# listing.
nfc-nfd-collision
# The same collision spelled identically.
duplicate-name
# One response past listingMaxEntries. Refused, never truncated: a silently
# shortened listing looks complete, and the file that fell off it is never
# delivered.
entries-over-cap
# One byte past listingMaxBytes.
bytes-over-limit
# An entity DECLARATION of any kind is refused outright — that is fail-closed
# against billion-laughs. The app switches off EXTERNAL entity resolution and
# lets Foundation expand an internal one, so it may well accept this body.
# Refusing more than the client is the safe direction for a checker; accepting
# more is the one that mints a setup code for a lane that never delivers.
entity-declaration
